question: Is there employment in occupations that are AI-exposed but not computer-desk work? That cell is what a horse race between AI exposure and computerization is identified from.
proxy_warning: Dingel-Neiman teleworkability stands in for computer-based work. It is NOT routine-task intensity and NOT Frey-Osborne computerisability. Re-run against Webb (2020), Frey-Osborne and a constructed RTI before the design freeze.

identification.note: This is the statistic that bears on whether a joint AI-plus-computerization model is identified. The conditional MDE is the measured unconditional MDE inflated by sqrt(VIF) and the null-size correction; it is an ESTIMATE and must be replaced by a simulation on the observed joint distribution before the freeze.

AIOE_Felten.verdict_note: 42.1% of this measure's employment-weighted variance is orthogonal to the computer proxy; adding the control inflates the standard error by 1.54x, putting the conditional MDE near 5.63% against a contested magnitude of 19% -- headroom of 3.4x. The discretized clean cell (1.61% of employment) is a descriptive aid, not the identification statistic.
